You are an INDEPENDENT, IMPARTIAL THIRD-PARTY AUDITOR. You did not write the document
and you have no stake in its conclusions. Your client wants to know two things:

  (Q1) FAIRNESS: was the measurement process fair and unbiased? Is the comparison
       apples-to-apples, or is the "before" case handicapped / the "after" case flattered?
  (Q2) REPRODUCIBILITY: can a third party regenerate these results from what is on disk
       and what is documented?

Working directory: /home/nick/work/llama.cpp
Document under audit: /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/profiling_gemm_27b.md  (read it in full FIRST)

PRIMARY EVIDENCE available to you (use it - do not trust the document's own words):
  - /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/sweep-gemm-27b/*.log   48 raw run logs: {pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k{48..59}.log
  - /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/sweep-gemm/*.log       4B prefill logs

  - /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/verify.sh /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/measure.sh /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/check-prefetch.sh /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/check-vd4dots.sh
  - /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/     the kernel source (arch/riscv/repack.cpp, arch/riscv/quants.c, ggml-cpu.c)
  - git history (branch q1_0-rvv-opt), git log/show/diff
  - sibling docs: profiling_gemv_27b.md, opt_roadmap.md, q1_0_reproduce.md

A log line looks like:
  [roi] MUL_MAT #57 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [5120 x 1024] nrows=4
  [andesim] 1630251 cycles

HARD RULE - DO NOT RUN LONG SIMULATIONS. A single RTL leg can take up to 20 HOURS.
Never invoke the simulator, never run a full 'bash sweep.sh' sweep, never build the model.
You MAY run: reading files, grep/awk/sed, git commands, arithmetic (python3/awk),
and cheap re-derivation from logs already on disk (e.g. 'bash sweep.sh --md' which only
re-formats existing logs - check the script first to confirm it does not launch runs).

RULES OF EVIDENCE:
  - Every finding must cite the exact file/line/log/command that establishes it.
  - Quote the document's claim verbatim in claim_in_doc.
  - Report BOTH what checks out and what does not. An audit that only lists problems is
    as useless as one that only praises. Populate verified_ok generously.
  - Do not speculate. If you cannot verify something with the evidence at hand, mark it
    'unverifiable' and say precisely what evidence would be needed.
  - Severity: critical = a headline number is wrong or the comparison is rigged;
    major = a real methodological bias or a blocked reproduction;
    minor = imprecision that does not change a conclusion; info = an observation.


LENS 5 - REPRODUCIBILITY, TESTED NOT ASSUMED.

Put yourself in the shoes of an outsider handed this repo. Test the documented path:
  1. Read sweep.sh and confirm what '--md' does. If (and only if) it merely re-formats logs
     already on disk without launching any simulation, RUN the three documented commands:
       MODEL=27b NODES="48 49 50 51 52 53 54 55" bash sweep.sh --md
       MODEL=27b NODES="56 57 58 59"             bash sweep.sh --md
       bash sweep.sh --md   and   MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh --md
     and DIFF the regenerated tables against the tables published in profiling_gemm_27b.md.
     Report any cell that differs. If --md would launch a run, do NOT run it - say so.
  2. Run 'bash sweep.sh --selfcheck' if and only if it is cheap (read it first). Report what
     it actually gates and whether it is a meaningful check or a tautology.
  3. Is the environment pinned? Engine version (vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3), toolchain version,
     llama.cpp commit, model file hash. Could someone else get the same numbers, or are
     there unpinned inputs? Check whether the doc/repro instructions name a commit; check
     'git log' and whether the working tree was dirty when the logs were produced (compare
     log mtimes to commit dates - 'ls --full-time', 'git log --format=%cd').
  4. Is the model file present and identified (name, size, hash)? Is it obtainable?
  5. Are the four builds reconstructible from what is documented? Find the actual build
     script/commands and check the doc gives enough to rebuild each variant.
  6. The document says layer 7 ffn_* rows are "carried" from layer 6 and that this is
     "sound". Is the carry documented well enough that a reader knows those three rows are
     NOT measurements of layer 7? Are they visually marked as inferred in the tables
     themselves, or only in prose? They feed the layer-7 geomean and the LAYER total -
     recompute layer 7's geomean WITHOUT the three carried rows and report the difference.
  7. Overall: grade reproducibility as (a) fully reproducible from disk, (b) tables
     reproducible but raw runs not, (c) not reproducible - and justify.

1	# Bonsai-27B prefill: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node, SSM and attention layers
2	
3	The prefill/gemm counterpart of `profiling_gemv_27b.md`, which covers the same
4	27B nodes on the decode/gemv path. Same engine, same nodes, same four build
5	stages -- `nrows=4` instead of `nrows=2`.
6	
7	Generated 2026-08-31. Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one
8	MUL_MAT node; nothing here is inferred except layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows,
9	which are noted where they appear. Regenerate any table with
10	`MODEL=27b NODES="..." bash sweep.sh --md`.
11	
12	## Setup
13	
14	| | |
15	|---|---|
16	| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
17	| Model | `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen35, 64 layers, 3.80 GB, 1.125 bits/weight |
18	| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--no-mmap --mem-size 12G -t 1` |
19	| Path | prefill / gemm, `nrows=4` (asserted per leg from the `[roi]` line) |
20	| Layer mix | `full_attention_interval=4`: 48 SSM layers, 16 attention layers |
21	
22	Every layer in the model is one of two kinds, so measuring one of each covers
23	the whole model: **layer 6** is an SSM layer (48 of 64) and **layer 7** is an
24	attention layer (16 of 64).
25	
26	| name | flags | meaning |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
29	| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |
30	| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
31	| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
32	
33	## Layer 6 -- an SSM layer (48 of 64)
34	
35	| layer | node | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
36	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
37	| 6 | `attn_qkv` | 5120 x 10240 | 52,428,800 | 181,789,774 | 27,118,723 | 25,385,875 | 8,976,703 | 20.25x |
38	| 6 | `ssm_alpha` | 5120 x 48 | 245,760 | 936,969 | 939,289 | 939,798 | 938,688 | 1.00x |
39	| 6 | `ssm_beta` | 5120 x 48 | 245,760 | 949,957 | 947,611 | 947,471 | 945,595 | 1.00x |
40	| 6 | `attn_gate` | 5120 x 6144 | 31,457,280 | 109,087,879 | 16,595,177 | 15,548,729 | 5,708,128 | 19.11x |
41	| 6 | `ssm_out` | 6144 x 5120 | 31,457,280 | 122,621,082 | 17,362,812 | 16,461,292 | 6,500,681 | 18.86x |
42	| 6 | `ffn_gate` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,587,645 | 45,434,691 | 42,133,870 | 14,351,598 | 21.57x |
43	| 6 | `ffn_up` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,915,506 | 45,437,135 | 42,135,770 | 14,349,546 | 21.60x |
44	| 6 | `ffn_down` | 17408 x 5120 | 89,128,960 | 382,982,019 | 47,880,022 | 44,881,677 | 17,064,993 | 22.44x |
45	| | **LAYER** | | **383,221,760** | **1,417,870,831** | **201,715,460** | **188,434,482** | **68,835,932** | |
46	
47	Geometric mean over the layer's 6 optimizable nodes: **20.60x**. `ssm_alpha`
48	and `ssm_beta` are excluded from every average in this document, for the reason
49	given directly below.
50	
51	Per-stage speedup:
52	
53	| layer | node | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | **total** |
54	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
55	| 6 | `attn_qkv` | 6.70x | 1.07x | 2.83x | **20.25x** |
56	| 6 | `ssm_alpha` | 1.00x | 1.00x | 1.00x | **1.00x** |
57	| 6 | `ssm_beta` | 1.00x | 1.00x | 1.00x | **1.00x** |
58	| 6 | `attn_gate` | 6.57x | 1.07x | 2.72x | **19.11x** |
59	| 6 | `ssm_out` | 7.06x | 1.05x | 2.53x | **18.86x** |
60	| 6 | `ffn_gate` | 6.81x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.57x** |
61	| 6 | `ffn_up` | 6.82x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.60x** |
62	| 6 | `ffn_down` | 8.00x | 1.07x | 2.63x | **22.44x** |
63	
64	`ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` are the only two tensors in the model the kernel is
65	never applied to. The dispatch gate at `repack.cpp:4889` requires
66	`cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0` -- the row-parallel kernel puts 64 rows in 64 vector
67	lanes -- and both have 48 rows. The `if` is false, no repack happens, and all
68	four builds run the identical stock kernel, which is why their four cycle
69	counts agree to 0.3% and their speedup is exactly 1.00x. Nothing was applied,
70	so they measure nothing about the optimization and are left out of every
71	average here. They are 0.12% of the layer's weights; padding them to 64 rows
72	would bring them in.
73	
74	## Layer 7 -- an attention layer (16 of 64)
75	
76	| layer | node | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
77	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
78	| 7 | `attn_q` | 5120 x 12288 | 62,914,560 | 221,201,927 | 32,315,274 | 30,372,677 | 10,662,439 | 20.75x |
79	| 7 | `attn_v` | 5120 x 1024 | 5,242,880 | 18,582,438 | 3,434,839 | 3,268,543 | 1,630,251 | 11.40x |
80	| 7 | `attn_k` | 5120 x 1024 | 5,242,880 | 18,575,271 | 3,432,110 | 3,268,500 | 1,628,900 | 11.40x |
81	| 7 | `attn_output` | 6144 x 5120 | 31,457,280 | 119,759,239 | 17,118,167 | 16,275,722 | 6,337,136 | 18.90x |
82	| 7 | `ffn_gate` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,587,645 | 45,434,691 | 42,133,870 | 14,351,598 | 21.57x |
83	| 7 | `ffn_up` | 5120 x 17408 | 89,128,960 | 309,915,506 | 45,437,135 | 42,135,770 | 14,349,546 | 21.60x |
84	| 7 | `ffn_down` | 17408 x 5120 | 89,128,960 | 382,982,019 | 47,880,022 | 44,881,677 | 17,064,993 | 22.44x |
85	| | **LAYER** | | **372,244,480** | **1,380,604,045** | **241,152,929** | **225,336,152** | **66,024,863** | |
86	
87	Geometric mean over the layer's 7 nodes: **17.65x** -- lower than layer 6's
88	20.60x, but not for the same reason: layer 7 has no gate failures. It owns
89	`attn_v` and `attn_k`, the two 1024-row tensors that stop at 11.40x because the
90	per-call activation quantize dominates when there are only 16 row tiles to
91	spread it over.
92	
93	Layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows are the same tensor shapes as layer 6's and are
94	carried from them, exactly as `profiling_gemv_27b.md` does for decode. The
95	carry is sound: `ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` are themselves the same shape and were
96	measured **0.11%** apart at upstream and **0.01%** apart at `d4`.
97	
98	Per-stage speedup:
99	
100	| layer | node | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | **total** |
101	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
102	| 7 | `attn_q` | 6.85x | 1.06x | 2.85x | **20.75x** |
103	| 7 | `attn_v` | 5.41x | 1.05x | 2.00x | **11.40x** |
104	| 7 | `attn_k` | 5.41x | 1.05x | 2.01x | **11.40x** |
105	| 7 | `attn_output` | 7.00x | 1.05x | 2.57x | **18.90x** |
106	| 7 | `ffn_gate` | 6.81x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.57x** |
107	| 7 | `ffn_up` | 6.82x | 1.08x | 2.94x | **21.60x** |
108	| 7 | `ffn_down` | 8.00x | 1.07x | 2.63x | **22.44x** |
109	
110	## Where the prefill speedup comes from
111	
112	All figures are geometric means over nodes, with `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta`
113	excluded. Decode has only five nodes measured at all four stages, so the
114	head-to-head below uses **those same five on both sides** -- `attn_gate`,
115	`ssm_out`, `ffn_gate`, `ffn_up`, `ffn_down`:
116	
117	| step | 27B gemm (prefill) | 27B gemv (decode) |
118	|---|---:|---:|
119	| upstream to +repack | **7.04x** | 2.24x |
120	| +repack to +prefetch | **1.07x** | 1.60x |
121	| +prefetch to +vd4dots | **2.75x** | 3.54x |
122	| **total** | **20.67x** | **12.64x** |
123	
124	Over prefill's full set of 10 optimizable nodes the totals are 6.62x / 1.06x /
125	2.58x = **18.15x**, against decode's 10-node figure of 12.20x.
126	
127	Per layer:
128	
129	| | gemm | gemv |
130	|---|---:|---:|
131	| layer 6 (SSM), 6 nodes | **20.60x** | 12.53x |
132	| layer 7 (attention), 7 nodes | **17.65x** | 12.17x |
133	
134	Layer 7 is lower on both paths because it owns the two 1024-row tensors.
135	
136	This reproduces the 4B prefill result (6.11x / 1.04x / 2.46x) on a model 6.5x
137	larger with a different architecture. Prefill takes its win from the **layout**;
138	decode takes its win from **prefetch and the dot instruction**.
139	
140	The absolute cycles show it without any ratio. On `ffn_gate` at `+repack`:
141	
142	| path | tokens | cycles | per token |
143	|---|---:|---:|---:|
144	| decode | 2 | 73,356,044 | 36,678,022 |
145	| prefill | 4 | **45,434,691** | **11,358,673** |
146	
147	Prefill does twice the tokens in 62% of the cycles -- 3.2x cheaper per token --
148	because the gemm loads each weight vector once and fires four dots against it
149	(`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`), while the gemv reloads it per token.

151	## Why prefill loses its edge on small tensors: a scalar activation quantizer
152	
153	Measured on Bonsai-4B, whose layer-7 nodes `attn_q`, `attn_v`, `attn_k`,
154	`ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` all share `ne0 = 2560` and differ only in row count, so
155	a node's cost splits cleanly into a per-call constant and a per-64-row-tile
156	term. Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%):
157	
158	| | fixed per call `F` | per tile `T` | per tile **per token** |
159	|---|---:|---:|---:|
160	| gemv `d4` (2 tok) | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
161	| gemm `d4` (4 tok) | 489,581 | 23,036 | **5,759** |
162	
163	In steady state the gemm is **1.88x more efficient per token**, exactly as the
164	M-tile sharing predicts. But it carries **12.4x the per-call fixed cost**, and
165	that constant is what decides the small nodes: `F` is 59% of 4B `attn_v`'s
166	total and only 12% of its `ffn_gate`. The same mechanism is why 27B `attn_v`
167	and `attn_k` stop at 11.40x while every larger node reaches 18.9-22.4x.
168	
169	`F` is not part of the kernel. Fitting the same model to every repack variant:
170	
171	| variant | gemm `F` | gemm `T` | gemv `F` | gemv `T` |
172	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
173	| `baseline` | 398,003 | 80,915 | 13,379 | 133,082 |
174	| `prefetch` | 441,355 | 76,544 | 27,294 | 85,084 |
175	| `d4` | 489,581 | 23,036 | 39,491 | 21,638 |
176	
177	`T` collapses 3.5x (gemm) and 6.2x (gemv) as the kernel improves; `F` stays put,
178	and stays an order of magnitude apart between the two paths. It is the shared
179	activation path, and the source says what it is. `forward_mul_mat` quantizes
180	activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`), and the routine it
181	picks depends on the token count:
182	
183	- **4 tokens** (`ne11 - ne11 % 4 == 4`) take
184	  `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>`, which selects
185	  `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` -- a **pure scalar** loop
186	  (`repack.cpp:51`, its own comment says `// scalar`): per 32-column block, 128
187	  `fabsf` for the amax scan plus 128 `roundf` plus the de-interleave index
188	  arithmetic. Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
189	  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
190	- **2 tokens** are not a multiple of 4, so they fall through to `from_float` =
191	  `quantize_row_q8_0`, which **is** RVV-vectorized on RISC-V
192	  (`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`).
193	
194	So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the
195	whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap, and at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest
196	single item in a small prefill matmul -- bigger than the kernel it feeds.
197	Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win.
198

201	| layer | node | prefill | decode |
202	|---|---|---:|---:|
203	| 6 | `attn_qkv` | **20.25x** | 12.03x |
204	| 6 | `ssm_alpha` | 1.00x | 1.00x |
205	| 6 | `ssm_beta` | 1.00x | 1.00x |
206	| 6 | `attn_gate` | **19.11x** | 11.86x |
207	| 6 | `ssm_out` | **18.86x** | 12.94x |
208	| 6 | `ffn_gate` | **21.57x** | 12.11x |
209	| 6 | `ffn_up` | **21.60x** | 12.11x |
210	| 6 | `ffn_down` | **22.44x** | 14.30x |
211	| 7 | `attn_q` | **20.75x** | 11.82x |
212	| 7 | `attn_v` | 11.40x | 11.24x |

216	## Notes
217	
218	- **`ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` get nothing on prefill either.** All four builds
219	  land within 0.3% (936,969 / 939,289 / 939,798 / 938,688). 48 rows fails the
220	  repack gate `ne1 % 64 == 0`, so every build runs the identical stock kernel.
221	  They are 0.06% of the layer's weights but **2.7% of its optimized cycles** --
222	  the same over-weight dead spot decode has, and worse in relative terms because
223	  everything around them got 20x faster. Padding them to 64 rows is the cheapest
224	  win available on this model.
225	- **Total speedup tracks node size.** `attn_v`/`attn_k` (1024 rows) reach 11.40x
226	  while everything from 5120 rows up reaches 18.9-22.4x. On the small nodes
227	  prefill gains **no more than decode** (11.40x vs 11.24x). The section below
228	  decomposes why.
229	- **Upstream is exactly linear in tokens.** Measured on all 12 nodes: 1.97x to
230	  2.01x for 2x the tokens. `.nrows = 1` (`ggml-cpu.c:257`) means one `vec_dot`
231	  per (weight row, token), so there is no prefill kernel upstream at all.
232	- **Prefetch is worth slightly more here than on 4B** (1.05-1.08x vs
233	  1.03-1.05x). 27B tensors are far larger than the 2 MB L3, so more miss latency
234	  survives the M-tile reuse.
235	- **`ffn_down` is the best node on both paths** (22.44x prefill, 14.30x decode).
236	  Its K=17408 is the longest reduction dimension, which punishes upstream's
237	  per-32-column horizontal reduction hardest.
238	- **`ssm_out` and `attn_output` are the same shape** (6144 x 5120) and agree to
239	  2.4% at upstream, matching the 2.6% decode spread that
240	  `profiling_gemv_27b.md` reports.

6	# once, one log per leg, so a killed or timed-out leg is re-run on its own

82	# Runs to completion, leaves everything in the log. Never parses; --report is
83	# the single parser, so a leg re-run and a fresh report cannot disagree.
84	run_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
85	  # Separate statements on purpose: bash expands every word of a `local` line
86	  # before it performs any of the assignments, so a log="...$v..." on the same
87	  # line would read an unset v.
88	  local v=$1 k=$2
89	  local log="$OUT/$v-k$k.log"
90	  local bin

93	  # below fails the leg dies instantly having done nothing, and 12 of those
94	  # look exactly like a fast successful sweep.
95	  mkdir -p "$OUT"
96	  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
97	    echo "SKIP $v k=$k: no $bin (run: ROI_K=$k bash build.sh $v)" >&2
98	    return 0
99	  fi
100	  # Resume: a leg that already produced both lines is done. Anything else
101	  # (empty, truncated, timed out) is re-run.
102	  if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then
103	    echo "have $v k=$k"
104	    return 0
105	  fi
106	  echo "run  $v k=$k -> $log"
107	  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
108	      --mem-size "$MEM" --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
109	      "$bin" -- -m "$GGUF" $MMAP -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
110	      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) > "$log" 2>&1
111	  local rc=$?
112	  grep -E '\[roi\] MUL_MAT|^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" | sed "s/^/    $v k=$k: /"
113	  [ $rc -eq 0 ] || echo "    $v k=$k: exit $rc" >&2
114	}

117	# One log -> "cycles<TAB>nrows<TAB>tensor<TAB>shape", or a reason it is not a
118	# number. Kept in awk so the nrows gate and the cycle read come from the same

120	read_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
121	  local log="$OUT/$1-k$2.log"
122	  [ -f "$log" ] || { printf 'MISSING\t\t\t\n'; return; }
123	  # [roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [2560 x 1024] nrows=4
124	  awk -v want="$WANT_NROWS" '
125	    /\[roi\] MUL_MAT/ {
126	      for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
127	        if ($i ~ /^src0=/)   { name = substr($i, 6) }
128	        if ($i ~ /^nrows=/)  { nrows = substr($i, 7) }
129	        if ($i ~ /^\[[0-9]+$/) { ne1 = $(i+2); sub(/\]$/, "", ne1)
130	                                 shape = substr($i, 2) "x" ne1 }
131	      }
132	    }
133	    /^\[andesim\] .* cycles/ { cyc = $2 }
134	    END {
135	      if (cyc == "")           { printf "PENDING\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
136	      if (nrows != want)       { printf "BAD-NROWS\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
137	      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", cyc, nrows, name, shape
138	    }' "$log"

160	# --------------------------------------------------------------- markdown ---
161	# The deliverable: the profiling_*.md table shape, generated from the logs so
162	# the document and the measurement can never drift apart. Reads the four
163	# stages BY NAME, so it does not care what order VARIANTS is in.
164	#   +repack    = upstream / baseline   (row-parallel 64x1 layout, F4)
165	#   +prefetch  = baseline / prefetch   (zicbop weight-stream prefetch, F7)
166	#   +vd4dots   = prefetch / d4         (nds.vd4dots.vv, F8+F9)
167	# A node missing any stage still prints its measured cells; only nodes with all
168	# four contribute to the geometric means, which is what "n =" reports.
169	md() {
170	  local k
171	  for k in $NODES; do
172	    local name shape cyc nrows nm sh v
173	    name=""; shape=""
174	    local -A c=()
175	    for v in pristine baseline prefetch d4; do
176	      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
177	      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
178	      c[$v]=$cyc
179	    done
180	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
181	      "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape" \
182	      "${c[pristine]}" "${c[baseline]}" "${c[prefetch]}" "${c[d4]}"
183	  done | awk -F'\t' -v mode="$MODE" -v nr="$WANT_NROWS" -v eng="$ENGINE" '
184	    function num(x) { return (x ~ /^[0-9]+$/) }
185	    # Group digits by hand. printf "%%%'"'"'d" would need a locale that defines a
186	    # thousands separator; under LC_NUMERIC=C it silently prints plain digits.
187	    function comma(v,   s, o) {
188	      s = sprintf("%d", v); o = ""
189	      while (length(s) > 3) { o = "," substr(s, length(s) - 2) o
190	                              s = substr(s, 1, length(s) - 3) }
191	      return s o
192	    }
193	    function fmt(x) { return num(x) ? comma(x + 0) : x }
194	    function rat(a, b) { return (num(a) && num(b) && b+0 > 0) \
195	                                ? sprintf("%.2fx", a/b) : "-" }
196	    BEGIN {
197	      printf "| layer | node | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |\n"
198	      printf "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
199	      n = 0
200	    }
201	    {
202	      split($3, d, "x"); w = d[1] * d[2]
203	      # ggml names weights "blk.<layer>.<node>.weight"; the row reads as the
204	      # model sees it (which layer, which matmul), not as the harness does.
205	      # K, the graph-order index, is a measurement handle and stays out of it.
206	      split($2, t, ".")
207	      printf "| %s | `%s` | %s x %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n",
208	             (t[2] == "" ? $1 : t[2]), (t[3] == "" ? $2 : t[3]), d[1], d[2], comma(w),
209	             fmt($4), fmt($5), fmt($6), fmt($7), rat($4, $7)
210	      # Geo mean over the fully-measured nodes the kernel can actually be
211	      # applied to. A tensor whose row count is not a multiple of 64 fails the
212	      # repack dispatch gate (repack.cpp, `cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0`), so every
213	      # build runs the identical stock kernel on it and it scores exactly
214	      # 1.00x. Including such a node does not report a weak result, it reports
215	      # a result about a different kernel -- and a geometric mean is brutal to
216	      # values at 1, so two of them drag a 20x layer down to 9.7x. The row is
217	      # still printed; it just does not vote. Same test as the gate, not a
218	      # hand-kept list of names.
219	      skip = (d[2] % 64 != 0)
220	      if (skip && num($4) && num($7)) ng++
221	      if (!skip && num($4) && num($5) && num($6) && num($7)) {
222	        n++
223	        lr = log($4/$5); lp = log($5/$6); lv = log($6/$7)
224	        sr += lr; sp += lp; sv += lv
225	        if (n == 1 || lr < mnr) mnr = lr; if (n == 1 || lr > mxr) mxr = lr
226	        if (n == 1 || lp < mnp) mnp = lp; if (n == 1 || lp > mxp) mxp = lp
227	        if (n == 1 || lv < mnv) mnv = lv; if (n == 1 || lv > mxv) mxv = lv
228	        tu += $4; tb += $5; tp += $6; td += $7
229	      }
230	    }
231	    END {
232	      # Summed cycles per stage, but NO ratio: sum(upstream)/sum(vd4dots) is a
233	      # cycle-weighted aggregate, which the big nodes dominate and which reads
234	      # like a per-node speedup without being one. Speedup is reported as a
235	      # geometric mean over nodes, below, and only there.
236	      if (n) printf "| | **ALL %d** | | | **%s** | **%s** | **%s** | **%s** | |\n",
237	                    n, comma(tu), comma(tb), comma(tp), comma(td)
238	      printf "\n### Where the %s speedup comes from (n = %d nodes with all four stages)\n\n", mode, n
239	      if (ng) printf "%d node(s) excluded: rows not a multiple of 64, so the repack gate rejects them and every build runs the stock kernel.\n\n", ng
240	      printf "| step | geo mean | min | max |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
241	      if (n) {
242	        printf "| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
243	               exp(sr/n), exp(mnr), exp(mxr)
244	        printf "| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
245	               exp(sp/n), exp(mnp), exp(mxp)
246	        printf "| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
247	               exp(sv/n), exp(mnv), exp(mxv)
248	        printf "| **total** | **%.2fx** | | |\n", exp((sr+sp+sv)/n)
249	      }
250	      printf "\nengine %s, nrows=%d (%s path)\n", eng, nr, mode
251	    }'

254	# --------------------------------------------------------------- selfcheck ---
255	# The harness gate. Two legs with values published in opt_roadmap (F8 for the
256	# prefetch build, F9 for the vd4dot one), run AT THE SAME TIME. Passing means
257	# the invocation measures what it claims AND that two concurrent hybrid runs
258	# do not disturb each other -- which is what licenses the parallel sweep.
259	selfcheck() {
260	  [ "$MODE" = gemm ] || { echo "--selfcheck has reference values for MODE=gemm only" >&2; exit 2; }
261	  mkdir -p "$OUT"
262	  run_leg prefetch 51 & local p1=$!
263	  run_leg d4       51 & local p2=$!
264	  wait $p1 $p2
265	  local rc=0 got
266	  # opt_roadmap F8: prefill K=51 prefetch 1,651,949 (an earlier session read
267	  # 1,649,275 on the same build -- 0.16% apart, so allow 1%).
268	  # opt_roadmap F9: prefill K=51 d4 818,314.
269	  for pair in "prefetch:1651949" "d4:818314"; do
270	    got=$(read_leg "${pair%%:*}" 51 | cut -f1)
271	    local want=${pair##*:}
272	    if [[ "$got" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && awk -v g="$got" -v w="$want" 'BEGIN{exit !(g>w*0.99 && g<w*1.01)}'; then

# Bonsai-27B decode profiling: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node (gemv path)

The decode/gemv half of the pair; `profiling_gemm_27b.md` covers the same 27B
nodes on the prefill/gemm path (`nrows=4`).

Generated 2026-08-25. All 15 matmuls of one SSM layer and one attention layer.
Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement except the three marked as
inferred from an identical shape.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
| Model | `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen35, 64 layers, 3.80 GB, 1.125 bits/weight |
| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--no-mmap --mem-size 12G -t 1` |
| Path | decode / gemv, `nrows=2` (confirmed per run by the `[roi]` line) |
| Node id | `ROI_K` = index of the MUL_MAT in graph order, 1-based, 497 per token |
| Layer mix | `full_attention_interval=4`: 48 SSM layers, 16 attention layers |

## Build variants

| name | flags | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel repack |
| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`, `Q1_VD4DOT=1` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |

`ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` are excluded: the repack dispatch gate

optimization.

| set | nodes | **geo mean** | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SSM layer (excl. the two gate failures) | 6 | **12.53x** | 11.86x | 14.30x |

| All 10 distinct shapes | 10 | **12.20x** | 11.24x | 14.30x |

The five nodes with all four stages measured.

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to standard RVV -- portable, any RVV core | **3.57x** | 3.33x | 4.11x |
| standard RVV to vd4dots -- Andes V5 XAndesVDot | **3.54x** | 3.47x | 3.59x |
| **total** | **12.64x** | | |

## Notes

- `ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` get **no speedup at all** (1.00x). They have 48 rows and
  the repack gate requires `ne[1] %% 64 == 0`, so both builds run the stock kernel.
  They are the only two gate failures in the model: 0.09%% of the weights but 1.7%% of
  the optimized cycles. Padding them to 64 rows would recover about 1%% of a token.
- Identical shapes give identical cycles **once optimized**. `ssm_out` and
  `attn_output` are both 6144 x 5120: 0.037%% apart at vd4dots, **2.63%% apart at

  prefetching one is not. K=60/61/62 are inferred on that basis, so their upstream

- Optimization compresses the spread. Upstream costs 1.75-2.14 cycles per weight
  across these shapes (22%% spread); vd4dots costs 0.144-0.158 (9%% spread).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 kernel A/Bs:
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   d4       = repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv kernels (XAndesVDot)
#   d4-nopf  = d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh d4                 # the vd4dots kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 shape table:
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                  : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK        : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON      : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                              gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON  : single switch for the vd4dot kernels - appends _xandesvdot
#                              to -march AND defines Q1_VD4DOT (kernels + sign-plane order)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N     : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack/vdot toggles   $3 extra defines (DIST etc., or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | d4 | d4-nopf | *-nodpref
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 = the shipped kernel with the K-reduction handed to nds.vd4dots.vv.
    # GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT is the whole switch: -march plus the Q1_VD4DOT source gate
    # (kernels and sign-plane repack order), so no extra define is needed.
    d4)       cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the vd4dot kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.
    d4-nopf)  cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-nopf$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|d4|d4-nopf|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

for t in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do build_one "$t"; done

Four checks, cheapest first. Each one proves a different claim from the
summit abstract; run them in order and stop wherever you have enough
confidence.

| level | proves                                   | needs                | time     |
|-------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------|----------|
| 1     | repack layout is numerically correct       | toolchain + qemu-user | ~1 min   |
| 2     | prefetch / `vd4dots` are actually emitted  | an existing build dir | ~1 min   |
| 3     | the shipped kernels reproduce upstream's text | andesim, fast mode  | ~8 min   |
| 4     | the cycle counts in the abstract           | andesim, hybrid + RTL | minutes/binary |

```bash

## Level 1 - repack layout correctness (qemu-user)

This checks the math, independent of the vendor instruction: pack random
weights, run the packed gemv/gemm, compare against a reference. Run it once
with the plain-RVV layout and once with the `vd4dots` layout - both must
pass, since they share the test and differ only in `VD4DOT`.

`o``bash

VD4DOT=1 bash build-vd4dot-qemu.sh   # vd4dots layout

overwritten by the second `build-vd4dot-qemu.sh` call, so run the test between
the two builds if you want to see both pass lines separately.

## Level 2 - confirm the instructions are actually emitted

Correct output doesn't prove the fast path ran - a silently-generic fallback
gives the same numbers, just slower. These gates disassemble the built

```bash

BUILD=b-prefetch ./check-prefetch.sh   # expects 2x prefetch.r per entry point
BUILD=b-d4        ./check-vd4dots.sh   # expects nds.vd4dots in gemv AND gemm,

## Level 3 - the shipped kernels reproduce upstream's output (andesim fast mode)

No RTL here. `--mode fast` is QEMU only - it stages the binary into a
`vlinux-run.elf`, boots `qemu-system-riscv64 -machine andes_ae350`, and
returns program output over semihosting. It runs the real model end to end
through `llama-completion` and compares the generated text of the two shipped
kernels against **upstream**:

| build      | flags                                       | role      |
|------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------|
| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`                       | reference |
| `prefetch` | repack + weight-stream prefetch (`DIST=1`)  | plain RVV |
| `d4`       | repack + prefetch + `nds.vd4dots.vv`        | XAndesVDot|

```bash
bash build.sh pristine prefetch d4   # if not already built
bash verify.sh                       # 4B model
MODEL=8b  bash verify.sh             # Bonsai-8B  (4G guest, --no-mmap)
MODEL=27b bash verify.sh             # Bonsai-27B (8G guest, --no-mmap)
MODEL=/path/to/other.gguf bash verify.sh
```

Expect one `PASS` line per build (fill in from your own run - the exact
continuation depends on the model):

```
model: .../Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf   ref: pristine   engine: vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3
PRISTINE: The capital of France is Paris. ...
PREFETCH: The capital of France is Paris. ...
PASS: prefetch output is identical to pristine
D4:       The capital of France is Paris. ...
PASS: d4 output is identical to pristine
```

The two comparisons are not worth the same thing:

- **`prefetch` should match exactly.** Upstream's `VLEN>=256` path
  (`ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_vl256`, `arch/riscv/quants.c:484`) reduces as
  `acc += d1*sumi` per q8 group, then `sumf += d0*acc` per block - and the
  repack gemv uses that same nesting. `prefetch.r` on top is an architectural
  hint and cannot change a result. So a mismatch means the repack layout or
  the prefetch helper's address arithmetic is wrong, never "the hint changed
  the answer".
- **`d4` (vd4dot) matching is a measured result, not a guarantee.** Its gemv keeps the
  nesting above, so decode is exact, but the vd4dot *gemm* folds `dx * ad[m]` into
  each q8 group and accumulates into `sumf` four times per block
  (`q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024`) where the others build `facc` across the groups
  first and accumulate once (`q1_gemm_64x1_vl1024`). Different rounding order,
  so **prefill** floats differ at the ULP level by construction. Equal greedy
  text is the acceptance bar; a future mismatch calls for a tolerance
  comparison, not a logic-bug hunt.

Two things that will silently weaken this check if you change them:

- **`--engine` is not cosmetic in fast mode.** It selects QEMU's `-cpu` and
  VLEN: `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` gives `andes-ax46mpv,vlen=1024`, while omitting
  it falls back to `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`. At 512 the vd4dot kernel
  (`q1_gemv_64_vd4dot_vl1024`) does not apply, `nds.vd4dots` never executes, and
  the comparison still passes while testing nothing. At VLEN 1024 the
  instruction genuinely runs - its decode is gated by `xandesv5isa`, which the
  fast-mode QEMU config enables.
- **This compares decoded text, not tensor bits.** Greedy argmax over 16
  tokens is a coarse filter: it catches gross corruption, not small numeric
  drift. Level 1's `test-repack-q1_0` is the numerical gate; Level 3 is a
  whole-model smoke test layered on top of it.

To isolate the prefetch hint on its own rather than the whole stack, use the
no-prefetch repack build as the reference instead:
`REF=baseline bash verify.sh prefetch` (needs `bash build.sh baseline`).

verified_ok.evidence: ffn_gate vs ffn_up 0.1059% upstream / 0.0143% d4 (doc: 0.11% / 0.01%); ssm_out vs attn_output 2.39% upstream (doc: 2.4%); 45,434,691/73,356,044 = 61.9% (doc: 62%); 36,678,022/11,358,673 = 3.229 (doc: 3.2x); upstream gemm/gemv ratio across all 12 nodes ranges 1.9724 to 2.0116 (doc: "1.97x to 2.01x"); ssm pair = 2.74% of layer 6's d4 cycles (doc: 2.7%).

verified_ok.claim: The four build variants are reconstructible.
verified_ok.evidence: build.sh is tracked in git and implements exactly the four flag sets the doc's variant table names (pristine = -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF; baseline = REPACK=ON + Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0; prefetch = REPACK=ON + DIST=1; d4 = + -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON). All 48 measurement binaries (bin-{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}[-k48..k59]) are present, and every b-*/CMakeCache.txt is retained, pinning the exact flags and the toolchain path. Toolchain identified from the binaries' .comment: GCC (2026-03-22_nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d-51225d7bd) 14.2.0.

verified_ok.claim: Log-to-binary chronology is coherent for 47 of 48 legs.
verified_ok.evidence: `stat -c %y` on all logs and binaries: 4B logs 2026-08-28/29, 27B logs 2026-08-30/31, binaries 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-24. Every log postdates the binary it ran, so no log was produced by a since-replaced build -- with the single exception of bin-d4-k59 (see findings). `git status --porcelain` shows no modified tracked files, so the source tree is clean relative to HEAD.

findings.title: Layer 7's +repack and +prefetch LAYER totals are wrong by 23.6%
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:85. Summed the doc's own seven layer-7 rows (lines 78-84) in python3: weights 372,244,480 (matches), upstream 1,380,604,045 (matches), +repack 195,052,238, +prefetch 182,336,759, +vd4dots 66,024,863 (matches). Cross-checked the +repack/+prefetch sums against the regenerated `MODEL=27b NODES="56 57 58 59" bash sweep.sh --md` ALL-4 row (56,300,390 / 53,185,442) plus the three carried layer-6 cells.
findings.finding: Two of the five bolded cells are arithmetically wrong. +repack should be 195,052,238, not 241,152,929 (published value is 1.2364x too large). +prefetch should be 182,336,759, not 225,336,152 (1.2358x too large). The other three cells in the same row sum correctly, and the identical row in the layer-6 table (line 45) sums correctly in all five columns, so this is not a definitional difference -- it is an error confined to two cells. The origin of the inflated numbers could not be traced to any other quantity in the document or in the logs.
findings.impact: No headline speedup changes: all published geomeans are computed per-node from the individual cells, and the LAYER row is never used as a ratio (sweep.sh:231-235 deliberately refuses to print one). But two bolded published totals are wrong by ~24%, and any reader who divides 1,380,604,045 / 241,152,929 to sanity-check the layer gets 5.73x instead of the true 7.08x.

findings.title: The doc's own regenerate command does not reproduce the layer-7 table or its 17.65x geomean
findings.claim_in_doc: Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node; nothing here is inferred except layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows, which are noted where they appear. Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES="..." bash sweep.sh --md`.
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:7-10, 87, 246-247. Ran the doc's exact layer-7 command `MODEL=27b NODES="56 57 58 59" bash sweep.sh --md`. Recomputed both geomeans in python3 from the log cycles.
findings.finding: The command emits 4 rows (attn_q, attn_v, attn_k, attn_output) and reports "n = 4 nodes with all four stages ... **total 15.02x**". The published table has 7 rows and reports 17.65x. There is no NODES value that regenerates the published table: k60/61/62 (layer 7's real ffn_*) were never run -- no such logs exist in sweep-gemm-27b/, which holds exactly 48 logs for k48-k59. Recomputed: layer 7's geomean over the 4 genuinely measured nodes is 15.02x; adding the three carried rows lifts it to 17.65x, a +2.62x / +17.4% increase. Note the document is internally inconsistent about this: its 10-node figure (line 124) correctly excludes the carried rows, while its per-layer figure (lines 87, 132) includes them.
findings.impact: Changes a headline number. Layer 7's published 17.65x is a 4-measured/3-carried blend; the measurement-only figure is 15.02x. It also propagates into the "Per layer" comparison table (line 132) and into the narrative "layer 7 has no gate failures" framing, which invites the reader to treat 17.65x as fully measured.

findings.title: The three carried layer-7 rows are not marked in the table, unlike the sibling doc they claim to follow
findings.claim_in_doc: Layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows are the same tensor shapes as layer 6's and are carried from them, exactly as `profiling_gemv_27b.md` does for decode.
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:76-96 (the raw markdown) against profiling_gemv_27b.md:35-56. Read both tables as text.
findings.finding: profiling_gemv_27b.md has a dedicated final column, `source`, and every carried row reads `inferred, = K53` / `= K54` / `= K55`, with the measured rows reading `4 stages` or `2 stages`. profiling_gemm_27b.md has no such column and no marker of any kind -- rows 82-84 are typographically identical to the measured rows above them, and they silently feed the bolded LAYER row at line 85 and the 17.65x at line 87. The disclosure exists only in prose at lines 93-96, AFTER the table, and the claim that this is done "exactly as profiling_gemv_27b.md does" is false in the one respect a reader relies on. The other three tables that reuse these numbers (lines 100-108 per-stage, 129-132 per-layer, 201-214 per-node) carry no marker either.
findings.impact: Does not change any number by itself, but it is the mechanism by which finding #2 is invisible to a reader. Three of the seven rows in the layer-7 table -- 43% of it, and 62% of the layer's weights -- are not measurements of layer 7 and nothing in the table says so.

findings.title: One of the twelve `d4` binaries is provably a different build from the other eleven
findings.what_i_checked: `stat -c %s` on bin-d4-k48..k59: all 10,352,568 bytes except bin-d4-k59 at 10,352,672. `readelf -W -S`: bin-d4-k56/57/58 and bin-d4 all have .text=0x58c744 .rodata=0c5648; bin-d4-k59 has .text=0x58c818 .rodata=0c56c8 -- 212 more bytes of code and 128 more of rodata. `stat -c %y`: bin-d4-k59 is 2026-08-07 07:47, every other d4 binary is 2026-08-19 or 2026-08-24. Dumped CMAKE_C_FLAGS from all 48 b-*/CMakeCache.txt: b-d4-k59 alone carries an extra `-DQ1_D4=1` (the pre-rename spelling of the vd4dot gate; HEAD commit f480bccff renames Q1_D4 -> Q1_VD4DOT). The k59 log (2026-08-31 08:22) postdates the binary, so this 08-07 build is what produced the number.
findings.finding: The `+vd4dots` column of the layer-7 table is not one build. bin-d4-k59 -- the binary behind attn_output's 6,337,136 cycles and its 18.90x -- was compiled from a source tree 12-17 days older than the other eleven, and its code section differs by 212 bytes. The ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K constant cannot explain this: k48 through k58 all differ in that constant and are byte-identical in size. The f480bccff commit message asserts "Structural change only - a rename, no behavior change", and the diff is indeed identifier-only, so a pure rename cannot account for 212 bytes of codegen delta -- meaning the k59 tree differs in something beyond the rename that is not in git history.
findings.impact: One cell of the d4 column is not from the same build as its column-mates. A same-shape sanity check bounds the exposure: ssm_out is also 6144 x 5120 and, measured on a consistent binary, costs 6,500,681 at d4 -- 2.58% more than attn_output's 6,337,136. If attn_output were re-measured at ssm_out's value its total would fall from 18.90x to 18.42x and layer 7's published geomean from 17.65x to 17.58x. Small, but it is an unpinned input inside a column the doc presents as one build stage.

findings.title: The entire 27B decode side has no raw logs on disk and no documented way to regenerate it
findings.what_i_checked: `ls -d sweep-*` lists only sweep-gemm, sweep-gemm-27b and sweep-gemv (4B decode). sweep.sh:68 computes `OUT=$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE-$TAG`, so 27B decode would live in sweep-gemv-27b/ -- that directory does not exist. `grep -rn 73356044 .` (the decode cycle count published at line 144) hits only profiling_gemv_27b.md and profiling_gemm_27b.md, never a log. `find -name '*.log' -newermt 2026-08-01` returns only the three directories above.
findings.finding: Every 27B decode figure this document publishes -- the "27B gemv (decode)" column (lines 117-122), the "gemv" column of the per-layer table (lines 129-132), the entire 12-row "Per-node comparison, prefill vs decode" table (lines 201-214), and the 73,356,044 / 36,678,022 row of the absolute-cycles table (lines 142-146) -- is transcribed from profiling_gemv_27b.md, which itself cites no log directory. The doc's own "Reproducing" section (lines 244-257) gives commands for 27B prefill and for 4B prefill/decode, and none for 27B decode. I was able to verify these numbers only for internal consistency (the geomeans recompute correctly from the sibling doc's own cells: 2.2352 / 1.5975 / 3.5385 / 12.6351 and 12.53 / 12.17 / 12.20), never against primary evidence.
findings.impact: Roughly half the document's comparative content rests on numbers no third party can regenerate from what is on disk. To fix, either ship sweep-gemv-27b/ or state in the Reproducing section which command and which run produced them. Evidence needed: the 27B gemv log directory, or the andesim invocations that produced those cycles.

findings.title: No commit, toolchain, simulator version or model hash is pinned; HEAD postdates every measurement binary
findings.claim_in_doc: | Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 | | Model | `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen35, 64 layers, 3.80 GB, 1.125 bits/weight |
findings.what_i_checked: `grep -nEi 'commit|sha|git|toolchain|gcc|md5|sha256|version' profiling_gemm_27b.md` -- zero hits on any of those terms. Same grep on q1_0_reproduce.md finds a hard-coded toolchain path but no commit. `git log --format='%h %cd'`: HEAD is f480bccff, 2026-08-27 15:02; the newest measurement binary is 2026-08-24 14:30. So no binary was built from HEAD, and none was built from 5d01611f1 (2026-08-07) either, since the d4 binaries postdate it by 12+ days -- they came from an uncommitted intermediate tree. Computed the hashes the doc omits: md5 Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf = cdeb26f2fff8e7ba8bb3a4f201450784 (3,803,452,480 B), Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf = ac2048785f2f04f4062e28e89b3d31f8 (572,270,624 B). Also: sweep.sh, measure.sh, verify.sh, check-prefetch.sh and check-vd4dots.sh are all untracked (`git status --porcelain` shows them as `??`); only build.sh is committed.
findings.finding: Four inputs are unpinned. (a) llama.cpp revision: the doc names none, and the source state that produced the binaries is not any commit in the history. (b) Toolchain: recoverable only by reading the binaries (GCC 2026-03-22_nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d-51225d7bd 14.2.0) or the retained CMakeCache files, not from the doc. (c) andesim/vsim engine version: nothing in the doc or in any of the 48 logs records it -- a run with a different --engine produces a log that is byte-indistinguishable in every field the harness reads. (d) The model: no hash, no size, no source URL for a 3.8 GB gguf that everything depends on. Separately, the harness itself (sweep.sh) is not under version control, so "the script that made this table" is not archived alongside the table.
findings.impact: An outsider handed this repo can regenerate the tables (the logs and binaries are here), but cannot regenerate the LOGS, because they cannot reconstruct the exact source tree, cannot obtain the model, and cannot confirm which simulator build was used. This is the binding constraint on the reproducibility grade.

findings.title: Fit quality is reported only for the path where it is good; the gemm d4 fit that produces the headline F has 5.2% residuals
findings.claim_in_doc: Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%):
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:156. Refit all six variant x path pairs by ordinary least squares over the five 4B ne0=2560 nodes and printed per-point residuals. gemv max residual: baseline 0.28%, prefetch 0.11%, d4 1.14% (the "1.1%" claim, right at the edge). gemm max residual: baseline 0.21%, prefetch 0.91%, d4 **5.19%** -- specifically attn_q +5.19%, attn_v -4.22%, attn_k -4.23%, ffn_gate -0.46%, ffn_up -0.49%.
findings.finding: The document reports residual quality for the gemv fits only. The gemm `d4` fit is the worst of the six by a factor of 4.5, and it is the one that yields F = 489,581 -- the number behind "12.4x the per-call fixed cost", "~490K cycles per node", and "F is 59% of 4B attn_v's total". Worse, the largest residuals land precisely on the small nodes (attn_v/attn_k, -4.2%) that the argument is about, so the two-parameter model is least trustworthy exactly where it is being applied. With only three distinct tile counts (16, 64, 152) across five points, the fit is close to determined and cannot distinguish a true constant from mild non-linearity.
findings.impact: Does not overturn the conclusion -- the 12.4x fixed-cost gap between paths is far larger than the residual, and the scalar-quantizer mechanism is independently confirmed in the source (repack.cpp:51 `// scalar`, gated vector twin, -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF in every CMakeCache). But the quoted precision of F (six significant figures) is not supported by a fit with 4-5% residuals, and the reader is given the impression the fit was validated when only half of it was.

findings.title: The carry justification omits the same-shape cross-check that would weaken it
findings.claim_in_doc: The carry is sound: `ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` are themselves the same shape and were measured **0.11%** apart at upstream and **0.01%** apart at `d4`.
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:94-96 and 238-240. Computed both same-shape pairs available in the 27B gemm data: ffn_gate vs ffn_up = 0.106% upstream, 0.014% d4 (as published); ssm_out vs attn_output (both 6144 x 5120) = 2.39% upstream, 1.43% baseline, 1.14% prefetch, **2.58% at d4**. Compared against the decode equivalent in profiling_gemv_27b.md: ssm_out 4,804,951 vs attn_output 4,803,183 = 0.037% at vd4dots.
findings.finding: Two same-shape pairs exist in the data and the doc quotes only the tight one to license the carry. The Notes section does mention ssm_out vs attn_output at 2.4%, but only at upstream, and frames it as matching decode's 2.6% upstream spread -- it does not say that on the gemm path the pair is still 2.58% apart at d4. This matters because profiling_gemv_27b.md's stated rule for inferring rows is "Identical shapes give identical cycles once optimized ... 0.037% apart at vd4dots", and on the prefill path that rule does not hold: the optimized spread is 70x wider than on decode. ffn_gate/ffn_up is a within-role pair and ssm_out/attn_output a cross-role one, so the tight number is not wrong -- but it is the more favourable of the two and the reader is not shown the other.
findings.impact: Bounded and small. Applying the worst observed same-shape d4 spread (2.58%) to the three carried rows moves layer 7's published geomean by well under 0.5x. The finding is about disclosure, not about the numbers being wrong.

findings.title: `--selfcheck` is a file comparison, not the concurrency gate it is advertised as, and its tolerance is 20x the stated noise floor
findings.claim_in_doc: bash sweep.sh --selfcheck     # gate: re-derive two published attn_v numbers
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:256. Read sweep.sh:259-280 and 84-114 before running. run_leg() resumes: if the log already has both a `[roi]` and a cycles line it echoes "have" and returns without launching anything (lines 102-105). Both target logs (sweep-gemm/prefetch-k51.log, sweep-gemm/d4-k51.log, both 2026-08-28) exist, so I ran it: output was `have prefetch k=51` / `have d4 k=51` / `PASS prefetch k=51 1651086 cycles (published 1651949)` / `PASS d4 k=51 823397 cycles (published 818314)`, rc=0, elapsed under a second.
findings.finding: Two things are worth flagging. (1) It is only cheap when the logs are already present -- on a fresh checkout the same command launches two RTL legs, which the doc's Reproducing section lists next to two genuinely free `--md` commands with no warning. (2) In the resumed state it is close to a tautology: it re-reads two files on disk and compares them to two constants hard-coded at sweep.sh:269, so it proves neither that the invocation measures what it claims nor that concurrent hybrid runs do not disturb each other -- both of which sweep.sh:26-29 explicitly claims it proves. Its 1% tolerance (sweep.sh:272) is also loose: the d4 leg passes at 0.62% off its reference, while the document's own stated run-to-run noise floor is 0.05% ("ffn_gate and ffn_up ... agree within 0.05%, which is the run-to-run noise floor here", profiling_gemv_27b.md). A regression of half a percent would pass this gate.
findings.impact: No published number changes. The gate is real when it actually runs a leg, and it did pass. But a reader following the Reproducing section will believe they have validated the harness when in the common case they have validated nothing, and may unintentionally start a simulation.

findings.title: Contradictory figures for the ssm_alpha/ssm_beta weight share (0.12% vs 0.06%)
findings.claim_in_doc: They are 0.06% of the layer's weights but **2.7% of its optimized cycles**
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:222, against the same claim at line 71 ("They are 0.12% of the layer's weights"). Computed from the doc's own weight column: (245,760 + 245,760) / 383,221,760 = 0.1283%. One tensor alone = 0.0641%. The cycle share checks out: (938,688 + 945,595) / 68,835,932 = 2.74%.
findings.finding: The same quantity is given twice with different values. Line 71's 0.12% is correct; line 222's 0.06% counts only one of the two tensors. Related minor imprecision at line 69: "their four cycle counts agree to 0.3%" is true of ssm_alpha (936,969..939,798 = 0.30%) but not of ssm_beta (945,595..949,957 = 0.46%).
findings.impact: No conclusion changes -- the point being made (a tiny weight share consuming an outsized cycle share) is if anything understated by the erroneous figure. But two published values for one quantity in one document is a copy-editing failure a reader will notice.

findings.title: The measurement invocation and the build step are under-documented for an outsider
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:18 against sweep.sh:71-72 and 107-110, and against build.sh. The actual guest invocation is `-m $GGUF --no-mmap -no-cnv --no-warmup --prompt "The capital of France" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1`, with `--step-timeout-ms $TIMEOUT`.
findings.finding: The Setup row names four of the invocation's parameters and omits the ones that decide which kernel is measured: the prompt text and `--no-warmup`. sweep.sh:16-23 is emphatic that the prompt is "the ONLY thing" that selects gemm vs gemv and that getting it wrong "still prints a perfectly plausible cycle count" -- yet the document, which is the artifact a reader will follow, does not state it. Also absent: any mention of build.sh, of the fact that ROI_K is compile-time (build.sh:27-29 explains andesim hands the guest an empty envp, so the node index cannot be an env var), or that 48 separate binaries are needed for the 27B sweep. A reader who runs only the two documented `--md` commands on a fresh checkout gets empty tables, and the only pointer to the fix is a stderr SKIP message inside sweep.sh:97.
findings.impact: Nothing published is wrong. This is the gap between "the tables regenerate" and "an outsider can run the experiment", and it is why the reproducibility grade is (b) rather than (a).

findings.title: Raw logs record almost no provenance
findings.claim_in_doc: Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node
findings.what_i_checked: Read sweep-gemm-27b/d4-k57.log in full (22 lines, as are all 48). It contains the staged ELF path (`app=/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4-k57`), llama.cpp's system_info line, sampler params, the `[roi]` line and the cycle count.
findings.finding: The logs do record which binary ran, which is the single most useful field and is what let me detect the bin-d4-k59 anomaly. But they record no engine string, no gguf path, no --mem-size, no timestamp, and no llama.cpp build id. Two runs on different engines, different models or different simulator versions produce logs that are identical in every field the harness parses. The engine, the model and the mem-size come from sweep.sh defaults (lines 46-54) and exist only as an untracked file's current contents.
findings.impact: No number is affected. It does mean the logs cannot self-authenticate: the Setup table's engine and model claims rest on the harness defaults, not on the evidence. One cheap fix would be to echo the resolved ENGINE/GGUF/MEM line into each log before the run.

findings.title: The document uses two different files under the same bare name `repack.cpp`
findings.what_i_checked: `wc -l` gives ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp = 5009 lines and ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp = 2204 lines. Resolved each citation against both files: 4889, 4456-4469 and 51 are in the generic 5009-line file; 1967-1972 is in the RISC-V one.
findings.finding: Bare `repack.cpp:NNNN` refers to the generic ggml-cpu/repack.cpp while `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:NNNN` refers to the RISC-V one, and both conventions appear in the same document without a note. My first attempt to check `repack.cpp:4889` against the RISC-V file returned nothing (it has only 2204 lines), which reads as a broken citation until you try the other file. Every citation does in fact resolve correctly once disambiguated. Separately, the gate at 4889 has three conjuncts (`__riscv_vlenb() * 8 >= 512 && cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0 && cur->ne[0] % QK1_0 == 0`) and the doc quotes only the row-count one -- accurate for the ssm_alpha/beta explanation, but incomplete as a description of the gate.
findings.impact: None on the numbers. A reader verifying the source claims will hit a false dead end.
